bug_semantics: The unauthenticated metatags GET handler accepts a caller-controlled url, validates only that it parses as a URL, rate-limits anonymous callers without requiring authentication, and passes the value to a server-side fetch. Because the fetch has no protocol/host/IP denylist and does not revalidate redirects, a remote caller can make Dub reach arbitrary external or internal services, including loopback, private-network, link-local, and cloud-metadata addresses; parsed title/meta data and response behavior are returned through the endpoint.
flaw_origin: Commit abe4c8e15ae21bd1db59f709aac874254536bbed first created pages/api/edge/metatags.ts. Its public GET handler read url from the query string, checked only new URL(url), then getMetadataFromUrl called fetch(url) and returned parsed metadata. Later moves and rewrites carried that same trust-boundary error through pages/api/edge/metatags.ts, apps/web/pages/api/edge/metatags.ts, apps/web/app/api/edge/metatags, apps/web/app/api/metatags, and finally apps/web/app/api/links/metatags; those later commits are not the BIC.
ai_marker: No AI marker. `git cat-file commit abe4c8e15ae21bd1db59f709aac874254536bbed` shows author and committer Steven Tey <stevensteel97@gmail.com> and only the subject `Added 3 types of social image previews: Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn`; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer in the BIC commit object.
evidence: Bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round9/case-alias-f4dd3d5362778772b5752334.json` identifies CVE-2026-72552/GHSA-gvqm-vjxp-3r33, describes unauthenticated SSRF through the metatags edge endpoint as of 2026-07-10, and contains no affected/fixed package-version entries (`vulnerabilities` is empty).

At default-branch HEAD 3462d79674bbe3c1161805d956111c2153fb4c6e (2026-08-27), `apps/web/app/api/links/metatags/route.ts` parses the query with getUrlQuerySchema, calls ratelimitOrThrow, then calls getMetaTags(url). `apps/web/lib/api/utils.ts:22-42` shows anonymous requests are rate-limited rather than rejected, while `apps/web/lib/zod/schemas/utils.ts:26-32` and `packages/utils/src/functions/urls.ts:1-7` show URL validation is only `new URL(url)`.

At the same HEAD, `apps/web/app/api/links/metatags/utils.ts:11-14,120-122` calls fetchWithTimeout(url) on the supplied value. There is no host/IP/scheme/redirect SSRF guard in that path. `apps/web/lib/middleware/api.ts:13-15` also rewrites public API-host paths under `/api`; it does not authenticate this route.

`git show --unified=80 abe4c8e15ae21bd1db59f709aac874254536bbed -- pages/api/edge/metatags.ts` reproduces the original flaw: the newly added handler takes `url`, performs only `new URL(url).hostname`, invokes getMetadataFromUrl(url), and that helper executes `fetch(url)` before parsing and returning metadata.

`git log -L 1,30:apps/web/app/api/metatags/utils.ts f42b9a957c0bce980dd243fb54ab31e0c6c0b834^` follows the predecessor fetch implementation back through the route migrations and ends at abe4c8e15ae21bd1db59f709aac874254536bbed. Independently, `git log --all --reverse -S'const metatags = await getMetadataFromUrl(url)' -- pages/api/edge/metatags.ts apps/web/pages/api/edge/metatags.ts apps/web/app/api/edge/metatags apps/web/app/api/metatags apps/web/app/api/links/metatags` begins at that same commit. Commit f42b9a957c0bce980dd243fb54ab31e0c6c0b834 is a later API path/helper move and rewrite, so it is rejected as the BIC.

Direct parent verification: `git ls-tree -r --name-only 317e3978cce47cd36734933529cf609cacac39b8 -- pages/api/edge` lists coordinates.ts, description.ts, links routes, and title.ts but no metatags.ts; `git diff-tree -r --no-commit-id --name-status 317e3978cce47cd36734933529cf609cacac39b8 abe4c8e15ae21bd1db59f709aac874254536bbed -- pages/api/edge/metatags.ts` reports `A pages/api/edge/metatags.ts`. The parent had separate title/description helpers, but the advisory's metatags endpoint and its combined response path did not yet exist.

`git cat-file commit abe4c8e15ae21bd1db59f709aac874254536bbed` gives the single parent 317e3978cce47cd36734933529cf609cacac39b8, human author/committer identity, and no AI-related trailer, establishing both that this is not a squash aggregate and that its commit-object AI signal is absent.

There are no repository release tags (`git tag | wc -l` returns 0), so Git cannot supply a semantic-version introduction or fixed-tag boundary. The first vulnerable commit is dated 2022-11-19; the vulnerable code remains on origin/main at 3462d79674bbe3c1161805d956111c2153fb4c6e, after advisory publication, so the public default branch is still unpatched rather than having a fixed version.

An unmerged remote branch documents an attempted closure: f6e9c6990013f18abdc873d8ce5d2a049d3de014 (`add ssrf-safe fetch wrapper for user-supplied urls`) changes the metatags fetch from fetchWithTimeout(url) to safeFetch(url), whose implementation allowlists HTTP(S), resolves and blocks private/reserved IPv4/IPv6 ranges, and revalidates redirects. However, `git merge-base --is-ancestor f6e9c6990013f18abdc873d8ce5d2a049d3de014 refs/remotes/origin/main` exits 1, while origin/security-ssrf-safe-fetch ends at 8eb1663c5a053dcba7ac0375eaf4fb337ef61b7b. Because the candidate fix never entered the default branch, neither fix_sha nor direct_fix_sha is claimed.
reasoning: The vulnerable product path is a public request-to-server-fetch data flow with only syntactic URL validation and rate limiting, so it matches the advisory's SSRF mechanism. History tracing rejects later moves/reimplementations and identifies the first creation of the metatags endpoint in abe4c8e15ae21bd1db59f709aac874254536bbed; direct tree comparison proves its immediate parent lacks that endpoint. The BIC is an ordinary single-parent human commit whose raw commit object contains no AI attribution signal, requiring NOT_AI under the BIC-only rule. The default branch remains vulnerable and has no release tags or advisory version range; the only repository-side SSRF-safe change is stranded on an unmerged branch, so null fix fields represent an explicitly unpatched case rather than missing research.
